summary: Repeals the 2001 Authorization for Use of Military Force (Public Law 107-40) effective 240 days after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals the 2001 AUMF but contains no provisions related to appropriations, budgets, or government expenditures. Any spending effects would be indirect and speculative through changes in military operations.
No provisions address tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to healthcare systems, coverage, or markets.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration policy, borders, or pathways.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.

The bill directly repeals the 2001 AUMF, which has served as the legal basis for numerous post-9/11 military operations. Removing this broad authorization constrains future military engagements without new congressional approval, creating a moderate link to reduced military activity and associated defense spending levels.
No provisions address environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs or social safety net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or choice programs.
No provisions address drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions address trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
No direct provisions on deficits or debt reduction; any fiscal effects are indirect at best.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No provisions address foreign aid levels or programs.
No provisions address voting access or election procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address labor rights or union policies.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
